```{r}
library(tsibble)
library(tsibbledata)
library(dplyr)

PBS

head(PBS) # function to see only the first rows, by default head() shows the first 6 rows
# had(PBS, 3) --> show only the three first rows


index(PBS) #this tells you the time variable --> asks : Which column represents time?

key_vars(PBS) #This tells you the grouping variables --> asks : "Which variables define the different groups in my time series?"
#the _vars is optional it allows R to show the keys in horizontal

# Find the first and last time points in the dataset:

min(PBS$Month) #first point --> the $ means "Give me the column/variable called Month inside PBS."

max(PBS$Month) #last point

# or both in once
range(PBS %>% pull(Month)) 

# Count the number of observations:

PBS %>% # %>% is called the pipe operator - it means "Take the thing on the left and pass it into the operation on the right."
  count(ATC1) #number of observations per ATC1 - "Take PBS, then count the observations by ATC1."

```


"fpp3" %in% rownames(installed.packages()) --> way to check if a package is already installed (here fpp3)

library() loads the package in the session

%>% ("pip") : this operator means "use this value for the following action"

example:
abs() %>%
log() %>%
mean()
--> here we will take the absolute value of the input, then we'll apply a log on this absolute value and finally computes its mean.
